text.p: Advance Bank of Australia shareholders on Monday approved the bank's proposal to reduce its share capital as part of its planned merger with St George Bank Ltd.
Advance Bank chairman Jim Service said shareholders representing 87.7 percent of the bank's issued capital voted in favour of the proposal, while 12.3 percent voted against.
Advance Bank shareholders earlier on Monday approved the bank's plan to change of its articles of association as a prelude to the merger with St George.
The change in the bank's articles of association allows a single shareholder to own more than 10 percent of the bank's shares.

Under the merger proposal, St George Bank is to offer Advance Bank ordinary shareholders 0.625 of a new St George Bank ordinary share, A$2.10 in cash from St George and a 20-cent per share special dividend for each Advance Bank share.
The special dividend would be franked to about 60 percent.
Advance Bank ordinary shareholders would also receive an interim fully franked dividend of 20 cents per share.
The offer values Advance at over A$2.6 billion.
